requirements.requirement: The system shall respond to parts search queries within 15 seconds.
requirements.source_citation: Honestly, it just needs to feel fast. But if you want a number, I guess for the parts search anything longer than, um, say fifteen seconds feels like forever when I'm on the phone.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states that a response time longer than 15 seconds for parts search is unacceptable, indicating a clear performance requirement.
requirements.follow_up_question: Are there specific parts search scenarios or data volumes that would make this response time requirement more challenging?

requirements.requirement: The system shall respond to repair facility search queries within 8 seconds.
requirements.source_citation: For finding a preferred repair facility, I expect it to be quicker—maybe eight seconds is reasonable.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder specifies that a response time of 8 seconds is expected for repair facility searches, setting a clear performance benchmark.
requirements.follow_up_question: What factors might influence the complexity of repair facility searches, and how would they affect this response time requirement?

requirements.requirement: The system shall generate audit reports within 10 seconds.
requirements.source_citation: The audit report needs to be something I can get before I move on. If I have to wait more than, hmm, ten seconds it interrupts my flow.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder emphasizes the need for audit reports to be generated quickly to avoid disrupting their workflow, specifying a 10-second limit.
requirements.follow_up_question: What are the typical sizes and complexities of the audit reports that need to be generated within this timeframe?

requirements.requirement: The system shall maintain an uptime of at least 98%.
requirements.source_citation: It needs to be reliable almost all the time. If it's down frequently people can't do their job. If you're asking for a metric, I'd say we need it up almost always, with very little downtime—maybe around ninety-eight percent uptime would be acceptable.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states the need for high system reliability, quantifying it as 98% uptime.
requirements.follow_up_question: What are the acceptable downtime windows for maintenance or updates, and how would they impact the 98% uptime requirement?

requirements.requirement: The system shall provide help and guidance contextually within 90% of the screens.
requirements.source_citation: It should be almost everywhere, like, you know, if I'm stuck I should be able to find guidance right where I'm working, not have to go to some separate manual. If I had to guess, maybe help should be available in the vast majority of screens—so users don't get stuck. I mean, ninety percent of the system having in-context help would be brilliant.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder emphasizes the importance of readily available help and suggests that 90% of screens should include in-context help.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific types of help or guidance are most needed, and how should they be integrated into the screens?

requirements.requirement: The system shall require no more than two days of onsite training for users to become comfortable.
requirements.source_citation: It can't be one of those big, drawn-out trainings. Most folks are busy, so it should be short and practical, done onsite with hands-on stuff. I'd say two days of onsite training should get people comfortable, but it should also be obvious enough that people pickup the basics quickly.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder specifies that training should be short and practical, with a maximum of two days of onsite training required.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific aspects of the system are most critical to cover in the training, and what are the expected outcomes for users after training?

requirements.requirement: The system shall integrate directly with the Choice Parts data feed to ensure real-time data synchronization.
requirements.source_citation: If it doesn't tap into the Choice Parts data directly we'll end up with old availability all the time. I mean, I've been on a call with a shop where they said a part was in stock, but our system didn't show it because someone forgot to update an export. That kills trust. So it needs to use the same feed we rely on now.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder explicitly states the need for direct integration with the Choice Parts data feed to avoid data staleness and ensure trust.
requirements.follow_up_question: What are the specific data fields and update frequencies required to maintain real-time synchronization with the Choice Parts feed?

requirements.requirement: The system shall support concurrent use by multiple adjusters during peak times, such as lunch rushes.
requirements.source_citation: When I'm in the office multiple adjusters are using it at once and it needs to keep up. Oh, and I forgot to mention, there's usually a lunch rush where everybody's trying to pull parts at the same time.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder highlights the need for the system to handle concurrent use by multiple adjusters, especially during peak times like lunch rushes.
requirements.follow_up_question: What is the expected number of concurrent users during peak times, and what specific system functionalities are most critical during these periods?

requirements.requirement: The system shall enforce role-based access control to ensure that users can only access data and functionalities appropriate to their roles.
requirements.source_citation: Within a company, people should see different things depending on their role—some folks need full view, others only the basics.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder emphasizes the need for role-based access control to ensure that users can only access data and functionalities appropriate to their roles.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific roles and corresponding access levels need to be defined, and what data or functionalities should be restricted for each role?

requirements.requirement: The system shall adhere to the company's UI guidelines to ensure consistency and intuitiveness.
requirements.source_citation: That's huge. If the layout, colors, and controls are different from our other corporate apps people get confused and make mistakes. It should feel like one of our apps so it's intuitive.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder stresses the importance of adhering to the company's UI guidelines to ensure consistency and intuitiveness.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific UI guidelines or design principles should be followed, and how can user feedback be incorporated to improve the look and feel?

requirements.requirement: The system shall provide undo or easy correction functionalities to accommodate user mistakes.
requirements.source_citation: It should be forgiving. People make mistakes, so undo or easy corrections are nice.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder highlights the need for the system to be forgiving and accommodate user mistakes through undo or easy correction functionalities.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific types of mistakes are most common, and what undo or correction functionalities would be most helpful?

requirements.requirement: The system shall provide notifications when a part's status changes.
requirements.source_citation: Notifications when a part changes status would be good, because I don't want to keep checking.
requirements.rationale: The stakeholder expresses the need for notifications when a part's status changes to avoid the need for constant manual checking.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific part status changes are most important to notify users about, and what notification methods (e.g., email, in-app alerts) are preferred?
